outcome: Make approved learning content easier to understand across Arabic, English, ability, and format needs.
overview: Manual localisation and accessibility remediation of learning content is slow, inconsistent and expensive, and learners who need Arabic, captions, audio or simplified formats wait longest. This solution transforms approved materials into reviewed translations, captions, audio narration, alt text and accessible formats while preserving learning objectives, terminology and source meaning. Bilingual human reviewers approve every item before publication, with automated terminology and WCAG-aligned checks in between. A 6–10-week pilot on an agreed content set targets a 40% reduction in approved localisation and remediation turnaround, measured against the institution’s own baseline, with every approval and version recorded for audit.

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (UAE, KSA); source content and derivatives stay in the institution’s tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: The institution does not own or license the source content it wants transformed
notFor.why: Machine transformation of non-cleared content creates copyright exposure the workflow cannot absorb

notFor.situation: No bilingual reviewers or accessibility owner available to approve output
notFor.why: The design requires human approval before publication — unreviewed machine output is not published

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the institution owns content rights, terminology and publication decisions · Duration: 6–10 weeks pilot; 12–20 weeks to a scaled service
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, localisation engineer, accessibility specialist; customer curriculum owner, bilingual reviewers, accessibility officer, LMS administrator · Support model: Business-hours support with term-time escalation cover; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Content inventory and rights confirmation
2) Pipeline and glossary configuration
3) Reviewer workflow co-design
4) Quality calibration on sample items
5) Pilot production run
6) Quality sampling and benefit review
